newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, but overnight rates soar.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, but overnight rates soar.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in moderate late trading on Friday, with rumours of a central bank intervention band widening remaining the focus, dealers said.
But they said overnight rates were volatile as rupiah suddenly disappeared from the market in the afternoon. Dealers were unclear of any specific reason for the tightness.
Overnight rupiah jumped to a high of 45 percent from 12.0 percent after opening at 16.5 percent in the morning.
One state bank dealer said the jump in overnight rates had nothing to do with fundamentals and was purely a mismatch.
"It's more technical than fundamental. We know some banks had unloaded rupiah earlier in anticipation of cheaper rupiah in the afternoon," the dealer said.
He said the usual pattern that rupiah was cheaper in the afternoon seemed to have encouraged some operators to unload early and cover back later.
"This seem to be a miscalculation because of the weekend and weekly tax payments factor. It was a tactical mistake."
Dealers said overnight rates softened to 40 percent later and might fall further but buyers seemed to have disappeared.
They said the jump was not linked to market speculation of a band widening although some said that was the reason rupiah was held back.
One local bank dealer said the sharp fluctuation also resulted from rupiah bidding by some state banks, followed by late entries of some foreign banks.
"They were squeezed because of a thin late market."
Tom/next swaps were biddish at 0.4/0.5 points.
Dealers said speculation of band widening continued to dominate dollar-rupiah trading. They said there were even rumours of an on-going central bank meeting linked to the band.

But they added the rumours were unfounded, helping the dollar to regain some ground on local support. Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,430.25/30.40 at 0930 GMT after strengthening to a high of 2,429.0 on the back of the band widening speculation.
Tomorrow was at 2,429.85/30.0. There is no trading in value today due to the U.S. Independence Day holiday.
Dealers were mixed over reasons for the band widening speculation. Some sourced it to an indirect recommmendation from the World Bank.
They said a wider band would allow Indonesia to be better prepared for possible external and internal shocks.
But others said pressure in the market was not really heavy and a widening would ultimately appreciate the rupiah which could then undermine the country's exports.
One chief treasurer said the band was becoming an efficient monetary tool at present if it was used with correct timing.
"I don't think it's the right time now because the band is not under any test. The central bank could spare it for a better time," the treasurer said.
One U.S. bank dealer said a band widening now would not be good timing in the wake of economic instability in Thailand.
Dealers said the rumours emanated from Singapore but had so far failed to convince local players.
One-month swaps were at 13.0/14.0, two at 27.0/28.5, three at 40.0/41.0 and six at 81.5/83.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,427/2,619 and the conversion band at 2,427/2,475 on Friday.
